result.summary: The street environment is characterized by narrow sidewalks directly adjacent to travel and parking lanes with no visible pedestrian crossing infrastructure. While sidewalks are present on both sides, the lack of marked crossings and the presence of parked cars creating visual obstructions increase risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crosswalks
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks visible at the intersection ahead, forcing pedestrians to cross without a designated or protected space.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Continuous on-street parking on both sides of the street blocks sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the image

hazards.name: Lack of sidewalk buffer
hazards.description: Pedestrians on the right sidewalk are walking immediately adjacent to parked cars and the travel lane with no physical separation.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions at the intersection to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past the line of parked cars.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a continuous sidewalk and mature street trees. Parallel parked cars line the curb, providing a physical buffer from traffic but also creating visual obstructions for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: A continuous line of parked cars obscures the view of pedestrians, particularly children, from drivers on the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line in the foreground.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at nearby intersections to improve visibility and shorten crossing distances.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to reduce vehicle speeds on this residential block.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with continuous sidewalks and parallel parking on both sides. While the pedestrian environment is functional, the lack of traffic calming and visual obstructions from parked cars are notable safety concerns.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curbside obstruct the view between pedestrians and approaching drivers, especially at potential crossing points.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the street in the foreground and midground.

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Roadway
hazards.description: The absence of lane markings on a wide street can lead to inconsistent vehicle speeds and positioning, increasing risk for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: The main roadway surface throughout the image.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade existing crosswalks to high-visibility continental markings to increase driver awareness.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow urban street with row houses and a small commercial frontage. While a continuous sidewalk is present, it lacks a buffer from the roadway and contains minor obstructions like a trash can and utility pole.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: A trash can and a utility pole narrow the effective walking width of the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground left and right side of the sidewalk

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or planting strip between the sidewalk and the travel lane, placing pedestrians close to moving vehicles.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Green Infrastructure
interventions.description: Installing street trees or planters would provide a physical buffer between pedestrians and traffic while improving the streetscape.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implementing curb extensions at the nearest intersection would improve sightlines and reduce the crossing distance for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Trash Management
interventions.description: Providing designated areas for trash receptacles to ensure the sidewalk remains clear for all users, including those with mobility aids.
